commands.set: View, change, reset, or save Baritone settings.
commands.modified: List settings changed from their defaults.
commands.reset: Reset one setting or all settings.
commands.goal: Set or inspect the current pathing goal.
commands.goto: Path to a coordinate or goal.
commands.path: Display or control the current path.
commands.litematica: Build a placement currently loaded in Litematica.
commands.come: Path to the player who issued the command.
commands.blacklist: View or edit the block blacklist.
commands.click: Use the targeted block or location.
commands.thisway: Path a specified distance in your facing direction.
commands.waypoints: Manage and travel to saved waypoints.
commands.sethome: Save the current location as home.
commands.home: Path to the saved home waypoint.

settings.allowbreakanyway: Blocks that baritone will be allowed to break even with allowBreak set to false
settings.allowplaceinfluidssource: Allow Baritone to place blocks in fluid source blocks
settings.allowplaceinfluidsflow: Allow Baritone to place blocks in flowing fluid
settings.allowinventory: Allow Baritone to move items in your inventory to your hotbar
settings.ticksbetweeninventorymoves: Wait this many ticks between InventoryBehavior moving inventory items
settings.inventorymoveonlyifstationary: Come to a halt before doing any inventory moves. Intended for anticheat such as 2b2t
settings.assumeexternalautotool: Disable baritone's auto-tool at runtime, but still assume that another mod will provide auto tool functionality
settings.autotool: Automatically select the best available tool
settings.blockplacementpenalty: It doesn't actually take twenty ticks to place a block, this cost is so high because we want to generally conserve blocks which might be limited.
settings.blockbreakadditionalpenalty: This is just a tiebreaker to make it less likely to break blocks if it can avoid it. For example, fire has a break cost of 0, this makes it nonzero, so all else being equal it will take an otherwise equivalent route that doesn't require it to put out fire.
settings.jumppenalty: Additional penalty for hitting the space bar (ascend, pillar, or parkour) because it uses hunger
settings.walkonwateronepenalty: Walking on water uses up hunger really quick, so penalize it
settings.strictliquidcheck: Don't allow breaking blocks next to liquids.
settings.allowwaterbucketfall: Allow Baritone to fall arbitrary distances and place a water bucket beneath it. Reliability: questionable.
settings.assumewalkonwater: Allow Baritone to assume it can walk on still water just like any other block. This functionality is assumed to be provided by a separate library that might have imported Baritone.
settings.assumewalkonlava: If you have Fire Resistance and Jesus then I guess you could turn this on lol
settings.assumestep: Assume step functionality; don't jump on an Ascend.
settings.assumesafewalk: Assume safe walk functionality; don't sneak on a backplace traverse.
settings.allowjumpatbuildlimit: If true, parkour is allowed to make jumps when standing on blocks at the maximum height, so player feet is y=256
settings.allowparkourascend: This should be monetized it's so good
settings.allowdownward: Allow mining the block directly beneath its feet
settings.acceptablethrowawayitems: Blocks that Baritone is allowed to place (as throwaway, for sneak bridging, pillaring, etc.)
settings.blockstoavoid: Blocks that Baritone will attempt to avoid (Used in avoidance)
settings.blockstodisallowbreaking: Blocks that Baritone is not allowed to break
settings.blockstoavoidbreaking: blocks that baritone shouldn't break, but can if it needs to.
settings.avoidbreakingmultiplier: this multiplies the break speed, if set above 1 it's "encourage breaking" instead
settings.buildignoreblocks: A list of blocks to be treated as if they're air.
settings.buildskipblocks: A list of blocks to be treated as correct.
settings.buildvalidsubstitutes: A mapping of blocks to blocks treated as correct in their position
settings.buildsubstitutes: A mapping of blocks to blocks to be built instead
settings.okifair: A list of blocks to become air
settings.buildignoreexisting: If this is true, the builder will treat all non-air blocks as correct. It will only place new blocks.
settings.buildignoredirection: If this is true, the builder will ignore directionality of certain blocks like glazed terracotta.
settings.buildignoreproperties: A list of names of block properties the builder will ignore.
settings.avoidupdatingfallingblocks: If this setting is true, Baritone will never break a block that is adjacent to an unsupported falling block.
settings.allowvines: Enables some more advanced vine features. They're honestly just gimmicks and won't ever be needed in real pathing scenarios. And they can cause Baritone to get trapped indefinitely in a strange scenario.
settings.allowwalkonbottomslab: Slab behavior is complicated, disable this for higher path reliability. Leave enabled if you have bottom slabs everywhere in your base.
settings.considerpotioneffects: For example, if you have Mining Fatigue or Haste, adjust the costs of breaking blocks accordingly.
settings.sprintascends: Sprint and jump a block early on ascends wherever possible
settings.overshoottraverse: If we overshoot a traverse and end up one block beyond the destination, mark it as successful anyway.
settings.pauseminingforfallingblocks: When breaking blocks for a movement, wait until all falling blocks have settled before continuing
settings.rightclickspeed: How many ticks between right clicks are allowed. Default in game is 4
settings.randomlooking113: How many degrees to randomize the yaw every tick. Set to 0 to disable
settings.blockbreakspeed: How many ticks between breaking a block and starting to break the next block. Default in game is 6 ticks. Values under 1 will be clamped. The delay only applies to non-instant (1-tick) breaks.
settings.randomlooking: How many degrees to randomize the pitch and yaw every tick. Set to 0 to disable
settings.costheuristic: This is the big A* setting. As long as your cost heuristic is an *underestimate*, it's guaranteed to find you the best path. 3.5 is always an underestimate, even if you are sprinting. If you're walking only (with allowSprint off) 4.6 is safe. Any value below 3.5 is never worth it. It's just more computation to find the same path, guaranteed. (specifically, it needs to be strictly slightly less than ActionCosts.WALK_ONE_BLOCK_COST, which is about 3.56)
settings.pathingmaxchunkborderfetch: The maximum number of times it will fetch outside loaded or cached chunks before assuming that pathing has reached the end of the known area, and should therefore stop.
settings.backtrackcostfavoringcoefficient: Set to 1.0 to effectively disable this feature
settings.mobspawneravoidancecoefficient: Set to 1.0 to effectively disable this feature
settings.mobavoidancecoefficient: Set to 1.0 to effectively disable this feature
settings.rightclickcontaineronarrival: When running a goto towards a container block (chest, ender chest, furnace, etc), right click and open it once you arrive.
settings.enterportal: When running a goto towards a nether portal block, walk all the way into the portal instead of stopping one block before.
settings.minimumimprovementrepropagation: Don't repropagate cost improvements below 0.01 ticks. They're all just floating point inaccuracies, and there's no point.
settings.cutoffatloadboundary: After calculating a path (potentially through cached chunks), artificially cut it off to just the part that is entirely within currently loaded chunks. Improves path safety because cached chunks are heavily simplified.
settings.maxcostincrease: If a movement's cost increases by more than this amount between calculation and execution (due to changes in the environment / world), cancel and recalculate
settings.costverificationlookahead: Stop 5 movements before anything that made the path COST_INF. For example, if lava has spread across the path, don't walk right up to it then recalculate, it might still be spreading lol
settings.pathcutofffactor: Static cutoff factor. 0.9 means cut off the last 10% of all paths, regardless of chunk load state
settings.pathcutoffminimumlength: Only apply static cutoff for paths of at least this length (in terms of number of movements)
settings.planningticklookahead: Start planning the next path once the remaining movements tick estimates sum up to less than this value
settings.pathingmapdefaultsize: Default size of the Long2ObjectOpenHashMap used in pathing
settings.pathingmaploadfactor: Load factor coefficient for the Long2ObjectOpenHashMap used in pathing
settings.maxfallheightnowater: How far are you allowed to fall onto solid ground (without a water bucket)? 3 won't deal any damage. But if you just want to get down the mountain quickly and you have Feather Falling IV, you might set it a bit higher, like 4 or 5.
settings.maxfallheightbucket: How far are you allowed to fall onto solid ground (with a water bucket)? It's not that reliable, so I've set it below what would kill an unarmored player (23)
settings.allowovershootdiagonaldescend: Is it okay to sprint through a descend followed by a diagonal? The player overshoots the landing, but not enough to fall off. And the diagonal ensures that there isn't lava or anything that's !canWalkInto in that space, so it's technically safe, just a little sketchy.
settings.simplifyunloadedycoord: If your goal is a GoalBlock in an unloaded chunk, assume it's far enough away that the Y coord doesn't matter yet, and replace it with a GoalXZ to the same place before calculating a path. Once a segment ends within chunk load range of the GoalBlock, it will go back to normal behavior of considering the Y coord. The reasoning is that if your X and Z are 10,000 blocks away, your Y coordinate's accuracy doesn't matter at all until you get much much closer.
settings.repackonanyblockchange: Whenever a block changes, repack the whole chunk that it's in
settings.movementtimeoutticks: If a movement takes this many ticks more than its initial cost estimate, cancel it
settings.primarytimeoutms: Pathing ends after this amount of time, but only if a path has been found
settings.failuretimeoutms: Pathing can never take longer than this, even if that means failing to find any path at all
settings.planaheadprimarytimeoutms: Planning ahead while executing a segment ends after this amount of time, but only if a path has been found
settings.planaheadfailuretimeoutms: Planning ahead while executing a segment can never take longer than this, even if that means failing to find any path at all
settings.slowpath: For debugging, consider nodes much much slower
settings.slowpathtimeoutms: The alternative timeout number when slowPath is on
settings.dobedwaypoints: allows baritone to save bed waypoints when interacting with beds
settings.dodeathwaypoints: allows baritone to save death waypoints
settings.chunkcaching: The big one. Download all chunks in simplified 2-bit format and save them for better very-long-distance pathing.
settings.pruneregionsfromram: On save, delete from RAM any cached regions that are more than 1024 blocks away from the player
settings.chunkpackerqueuemaxsize: The chunk packer queue can never grow to larger than this, if it does, the oldest chunks are discarded
settings.logastoast: Shows popup message in the upper right corner, similarly to when you make an advancement
settings.chatdebug: Print all the debug messages to chat
settings.chatcontrol: Allow chat based control of Baritone. Most likely should be disabled when Baritone is imported for use in something else
settings.chatcontrolanyway: Some clients like Impact try to force chatControl to off, so here's a second setting to do it anyway
settings.renderpathasline: Render the path as a line instead of a frickin thingy
settings.rendergoalanimated: Render the goal as a sick animated thingy instead of just a box (also controls animation of GoalXZ if {@link #renderGoalXZBeacon} is enabled)
settings.rendergoalignoredepth: Ignore depth when rendering the goal
settings.rendergoalxzbeacon: Renders X/Z type Goals as a no-depth beacon beam instead of the full-height goal box.
settings.renderselectionboxesignoredepth: Ignore depth when rendering the selection boxes (to break, to place, to walk into)
settings.renderpathignoredepth: Ignore depth when rendering the path
settings.pathrenderlinewidthpixels: Line width of the path when rendered, in pixels
settings.goalrenderlinewidthpixels: Line width of the goal when rendered, in pixels
settings.fadepath: Start fading out the path at 20 movements ahead, and stop rendering it entirely 30 movements ahead. Improves FPS.
settings.freelook: Move without having to force the client-sided rotations
settings.blockfreelook: Break and place blocks without having to force the client-sided rotations. Requires {@link #freeLook}.
settings.elytrafreelook: Automatically elytra fly without having to force the client-sided rotations.
settings.smoothlook: Forces the client-sided yaw rotation to an average of the last {@link #smoothLookTicks} of server-sided rotations.
settings.elytrasmoothlook: Same as {@link #smoothLook} but for elytra flying.
settings.smoothlookticks: The number of ticks to average across for {@link #smoothLook};
settings.remainwithexistinglookdirection: When true, the player will remain with its existing look direction as often as possible. Although, in some cases this can get it stuck, hence this setting to disable that behavior.
settings.anticheatcompatibility: Will cause some minor behavioral differences to ensure that Baritone works on anticheats.
settings.paththroughcachedonly: Exclusively use cached chunks for pathing
settings.blacklistclosestonfailure: When GetToBlockProcess or MineProcess fails to calculate a path, instead of just giving up, mark the closest instance of that block as "unreachable" and go towards the next closest. GetToBlock expands this search to the whole "vein"; MineProcess does not. This is because MineProcess finds individual impossible blocks (like one block in a vein that has gravel on top then lava, so it can't break) Whereas GetToBlock should blacklist the whole "vein" if it can't get to any of them.
settings.rendercachedchunks: 😎 Render cached chunks as semitransparent. Doesn't work with OptiFine 😭 Rarely randomly crashes, see this issue.
settings.cachedchunksopacity: 0.0f = not visible, fully transparent (instead of setting this to 0, turn off renderCachedChunks) 1.0f = fully opaque
settings.prefixcontrol: Whether or not to allow you to run Baritone commands with the prefix
settings.prefix: The command prefix for chat control
settings.shortbaritoneprefix: Use a short Baritone prefix [B] instead of [Baritone] when logging to chat
settings.usemessagetag: Use a modern message tag instead of a prefix when logging to chat
settings.echocommands: Echo commands to chat when they are run
settings.censorcoordinates: Censor coordinates in goals and block positions
settings.censorrancommands: Censor arguments to ran commands, to hide, for example, coordinates to #goal
settings.itemsaver: Stop using tools just before they are going to break.
settings.itemsaverthreshold: Durability to leave on the tool when using itemSaver
settings.prefersilktouch: Always prefer silk touch tools over regular tools. This will not sacrifice speed, but it will always prefer silk touch tools over other tools of the same speed. This includes always choosing ANY silk touch tool over your hand.
settings.walkwhilebreaking: Don't stop walking forward when you need to break blocks in your way
settings.splicepath: When a new segment is calculated that doesn't overlap with the current one, but simply begins where the current segment ends, splice it on and make a longer combined path. If this setting is off, any planned segment will not be spliced and will instead be the "next path" in PathingBehavior, and will only start after this one ends. Turning this off hurts planning ahead, because the next segment will exist even if it's very short.
settings.maxpathhistorylength: If we are more than 300 movements into the current path, discard the oldest segments, as they are no longer useful
settings.pathhistorycutoffamount: If the current path is too long, cut off this many movements from the beginning.
settings.minegoalupdateinterval: Rescan for the goal once every 5 ticks. Set to 0 to disable.
settings.maxcachedworldscancount: After finding this many instances of the target block in the cache, it will stop expanding outward the chunk search.
settings.minemaxorelocationscount: Mine will not scan for or remember more than this many target locations. Note that the number of locations retrieved from cache is additionaly limited by {@link #maxCachedWorldScanCount}.
settings.minylevelwhilemining: Sets the minimum y level whilst mining - set to 0 to turn off. if world has negative y values, subtract the min world height to get the value to put here
settings.maxylevelwhilemining: Sets the maximum y level to mine ores at.
settings.allowonlyexposedores: This will only allow baritone to mine exposed ores, can be used to stop ore obfuscators on servers that use them.
settings.allowonlyexposedoresdistance: When allowOnlyExposedOres is enabled this is the distance around to search.
settings.exploreforblocks: When GetToBlock or non-legit Mine doesn't know any locations for the desired block, explore randomly instead of giving up.
settings.worldexploringchunkoffset: While exploring the world, offset the closest unloaded chunk by this much in both axes.
settings.explorechunksetminimumsize: Take the 10 closest chunks, even if they aren't strictly tied for distance metric from origin.
settings.exploremaintainy: Attempt to maintain Y coordinate while exploring
settings.replantcrops: Replant normal Crops while farming and leave cactus and sugarcane to regrow
settings.replantnetherwart: Replant nether wart while farming. This setting only has an effect when replantCrops is also enabled
settings.farmusingselection: When enabled, farming will be restricted to the current selection.
settings.farmmaxscansize: Farming will scan for at most this many blocks.
settings.extendcacheonthreshold: When the cache scan gives less blocks than the maximum threshold (but still above zero), scan the main world too.
settings.buildinlayers: Don't consider the next layer in builder until the current one is done
settings.layerorder: false = build from bottom to top
settings.layerheight: How high should the individual layers be?
settings.startatlayer: Start building the schematic at a specific layer. Can help on larger builds when schematic wants to break things its already built
settings.skipfailedlayers: If a layer is unable to be constructed, just skip it.
settings.buildonlyselection: Only build the selected part of schematics
settings.buildrepeat: How far to move before repeating the build. 0 to disable repeating on a certain axis, 0,0,0 to disable entirely
settings.buildrepeatcount: How many times to buildrepeat. -1 for infinite.
settings.buildrepeatsneaky: Don't notify schematics that they are moved. e.g. replacing will replace the same spots for every repetition Mainly for backward compatibility.
settings.breakfromabove: Allow standing above a block while mining it, in BuilderProcess
settings.goalbreakfromabove: As well as breaking from above, set a goal to up and to the side of all blocks to break.
settings.mapartmode: Build in map art mode, which makes baritone only care about the top block in each column
settings.okifwater: Override builder's behavior to not attempt to correct blocks that are currently water
settings.incorrectsize: The set of incorrect blocks can never grow beyond this size
settings.breakcorrectblockpenaltymultiplier: Multiply the cost of breaking a block that's correct in the builder's schematic by this coefficient
settings.placeincorrectblockpenaltymultiplier: Multiply the cost of placing a block that's incorrect in the builder's schematic by this coefficient
settings.schematicorientationx: When this setting is true, build a schematic with the highest X coordinate being the origin, instead of the lowest
settings.schematicorientationy: When this setting is true, build a schematic with the highest Y coordinate being the origin, instead of the lowest
settings.schematicorientationz: When this setting is true, build a schematic with the highest Z coordinate being the origin, instead of the lowest
settings.buildschematicrotation: Rotates the schematic before building it. Possible values are   NONE - No rotation   CLOCKWISE_90 - Rotate 90° clockwise   CLOCKWISE_180 - Rotate 180° clockwise   COUNTERCLOCKWISE_90 - Rotate 270° clockwise
settings.buildschematicmirror: Mirrors the schematic before building it. Possible values are   FRONT_BACK - mirror the schematic along its local x axis   LEFT_RIGHT - mirror the schematic along its local z axis
settings.schematicfallbackextension: The fallback used by the build command when no extension is specified. This may be useful if schematics of a particular format are used often, and the user does not wish to have to specify the extension with every usage.
settings.buildertickscanradius: Distance to scan every tick for updates. Expanding this beyond player reach distance (i.e. setting it to 6 or above) is only necessary in very large schematics where rescanning the whole thing is costly.
settings.minescandroppeditems: While mining, should it also consider dropped items of the correct type as a pathing destination (as well as ore blocks)?
settings.minedroploiterdurationmsthankslouca: While mining, wait this number of milliseconds after mining an ore to see if it will drop an item instead of immediately going onto the next one
settings.distancetrim: Trim incorrect positions too far away, helps performance but hurts reliability in very large schematics
settings.cancelongoalinvalidation: Cancel the current path if the goal has changed, and the path originally ended in the goal but doesn't anymore.
settings.axisheight: The "axis" command (aka GoalAxis) will go to a axis, or diagonal axis, at this Y level.
settings.disconnectonarrival: Disconnect from the server upon arriving at your goal
settings.legitmine: Disallow MineBehavior from using X-Ray to see where the ores are. Turn this option on to force it to mine "legit" where it will only mine an ore once it can actually see it, so it won't do or know anything that a normal player couldn't. If you don't want it to look like you're X-Raying, turn this on This will always explore, regardless of exploreForBlocks
settings.legitmineylevel: What Y level to go to for legit strip mining
settings.legitmineincludediagonals: Magically see ores that are separated diagonally from existing ores. Basically like mining around the ores that it finds in case there's one there touching it diagonally, except it checks it un-legit-ly without having the mine blocks to see it. You can decide whether this looks plausible or not.
settings.forceinternalmining: When mining block of a certain type, try to mine two at once instead of one. If the block above is also a goal block, set GoalBlock instead of GoalTwoBlocks If the block below is also a goal block, set GoalBlock to the position one down instead of GoalTwoBlocks
settings.internalminingairexception: Modification to the previous setting, only has effect if forceInternalMining is true If true, only apply the previous setting if the block adjacent to the goal isn't air.
settings.followoffsetdistance: The actual GoalNear is set this distance away from the entity you're following
settings.followoffsetdirection: The actual GoalNear is set in this direction from the entity you're following. This value is in degrees.
settings.followradius: The radius (for the GoalNear) of how close to your target position you actually have to be
settings.followtargetmaxdistance: The maximum distance to the entity you're following
settings.disablecompletioncheck: Turn this on if your exploration filter is enormous, you don't want it to check if it's done, and you are just fine with it just hanging on completion
settings.cachedchunksexpiryseconds: Cached chunks (regardless of if they're in RAM or saved to disk) expire and are deleted after this number of seconds -1 to disable
settings.verbosecommandexceptions: Print out ALL command exceptions as a stack trace to stdout, even simple syntax errors
settings.ylevelboxsize: The size of the box that is rendered when the current goal is a GoalYLevel
settings.colorcurrentpath: The color of the current path
settings.colornextpath: The color of the next path
settings.colorblockstobreak: The color of the blocks to break
settings.colorblockstoplace: The color of the blocks to place
settings.colorblockstowalkinto: The color of the blocks to walk into
settings.colorbestpathsofar: The color of the best path so far
settings.colormostrecentconsidered: The color of the path to the most recent considered node
settings.colorgoalbox: The color of the goal box
settings.colorinvertedgoalbox: The color of the goal box when it's inverted
settings.colorselectionpos1: The color of the selection pos 1
settings.colorselectionpos2: The color of the selection pos 2
settings.selectionopacity: The opacity of the selection. 0 is completely transparent, 1 is completely opaque
settings.selectionlinewidth: Line width of the goal when rendered, in pixels
settings.elytrasimulationticks: The number of ticks of elytra movement to simulate while firework boost is not active. Higher values are computationally more expensive.
settings.elytrapitchrange: The maximum allowed deviation in pitch from a direct line-of-sight to the flight target. Higher values are computationally more expensive.
settings.elytrafireworkspeed: The minimum speed that the player can drop to (in blocks/tick) before a firework is automatically deployed.
settings.elytrafireworksetbackusedelay: The delay after the player's position is set-back by the server that a firework may be automatically deployed. Value is in ticks.
settings.elytraminimumavoidance: The minimum padding value that is added to the player's hitbox when considering which point to fly to on the path. High values can result in points not being considered which are otherwise safe to fly to. Low values can result in flight paths which are extremely tight, and there's the possibility of crashing due to getting too low to the ground.
settings.elytraconservefireworks: If enabled, avoids using fireworks when descending along the flight path.
settings.elytrarenderraytraces: Renders the raytraces that are performed by the elytra fly calculation.
settings.elytrarenderhitboxraytraces: Renders the raytraces that are used in the hitbox part of the elytra fly calculation. Requires {@link #elytraRenderRaytraces}.
settings.elytrarendersimulation: Renders the best elytra flight path that was simulated each tick.
settings.elytraautojump: Automatically path to and jump off of ledges to initiate elytra flight when grounded.
settings.elytranetherseed: The seed used to generate chunks for long distance elytra path-finding in the nether. Defaults to 2b2t's nether seed.
settings.elytrapredictterrain: Whether nether-pathfinder should generate terrain based on {@link #elytraNetherSeed}. If false all chunks that haven't been loaded are assumed to be air.
settings.elytraautoswap: Automatically swap the current elytra with a new one when the durability gets too low
settings.elytraminimumdurability: The minimum durability an elytra can have before being swapped
settings.elytraminfireworksbeforelanding: The minimum fireworks before landing early for safety
settings.elytraallowemergencyland: Automatically land when elytra is almost out of durability, or almost out of fireworks
settings.elytratimebetweencachecullsecs: Time between culling far away chunks from the nether pathfinder chunk cache
settings.elytracacheculldistance: Maximum distance chunks can be before being culled from the nether pathfinder chunk cache
settings.elytraallowlandonnetherfortress: Should elytra consider nether brick a valid landing block
settings.elytratermsaccepted: Has the user read and understood the elytra terms and conditions
settings.elytrachatspam: Verbose chat logging in elytra mode
settings.elytracustomallocator: May reduce memory usage by using a custom allocator for pathfinding
settings.elytraallowtightspaces: Allow the pathfinder to attempt flight in tighter spaces, useful in caves but can be dangerous.
settings.elytraallowaboveroof: Allow the pathfinder to fly above y 128 in the nether.
settings.elytrausecache: Allow the pathfinder to access the baritone cache to improve pathing
settings.elytraallowabovebuildlimit: Allow the pathfinder to fly above the build limit in the overworld and end.
settings.elytralongdistancethreshold: Minimum distance in blocks of an elytra trip before the pathfinder will try to fly above build limit. (Minimum: 32). Requires {@link #elytraAllowAboveBuildLimit} to be enabled.
settings.allowwalkonmagmablocks: Sneak when magma blocks are under feet
